Thesiger's hunting trophies from his first treks in Western Nuer District, arranged against a wall on the upper deck of the government steamer Kereri. To the left is Thesiger's Zaghawi servant Idris Daud, and to the right his interpreter Malo. Both accompanied Thesiger on hunting trips and were given guns of their own to use.

Mica to be made into pottery slip.
Blacksmith's nozzle for directing air blast: pottery cone. [L.Ph 'DCF 2004-2006 What's Upstairs?' 26/11/2004]
Clay with added filler ready to use for pottery

Stove. Made of beaten clay into a pedestalled bowl shape with 3 supports projecting inwards below the rim. Slipped with red haematite & mica, red on the interior with some scorch marks on the surface. Mat impression remains on the bowl, which is perforated. Patch of blue pigment on the exterior. [Alicia Bell [OPS move] 29/06/2016]

Small pottery figure of a camel with seat on back, painted with white lines. Stands on four legs, with a short tail and elongated neck. Head has pointed, conical nose, and two pointed ears standing upright. Raised section on back, representing the hump, and a curved seat on back. [IL [OPS Move] 25/5/2017]
Ablution vessel. Small shallow dish with rounded base, the outside covered with mud. [JP 29/3/2004]
Bowl of clay in spherical form with a wide mouth. Slipped with red haematite and mica, fired on its side for a red oxidised interior. There is also an impressed pattern visible.

Water pot, beaten out of clay and tempered with millet husk into spherical shape. The shallow flaring neck was coiled of clay with dung filler. The vessel was slipped with red haematite and mica and fired mouth down for a black interior. One vestigial handle adorns the neck-body junction; below this is a decorative 'chain' of impressions below which the pattern impressed on the body during its rotation on a fibre pounding mat. [ASh [OPS move] 09/03/2016]
Grass for use as a temper for pottery

Beer jar, with a spherical body beaten of clay tempered with millet husk, coiled raised straight neck of clay with dung filler, 2 vestigial handles. Slipped with red haematite & mica. A black mark on the side. Below the indented neck-body junction is a twisted coil pattern; below this a mat impression remains. A cross is etched within the neck & on one side of the body.  [ASh [OPS move] 09/03/2016]
Jar with spherical body of clay, coiled raised straight neck & 2 vestigial handles. [MOBB [OPS move] 04/02/2016]
Ink pot of clay. It consists of an inverted shallow cone joined to a spherical bowl with base. [MOBB [OPS move] 04/02/2016]
Bowl of clay, slipped with red haematite and mica, and fired on its side. [MOBB [OPS move] 04/02/2016]
Small bowl of clay in a spherical wide-mouthed shape. The interior & upper body are coated with an especially micaceous slip.

Water jug, with a spherical body beaten out of clay tempered with millet husk, with a coiled base, flaring trumpet neck, handle, and a plug spout. Beneath the rim a perforated top is built into the neck; the end of the spout is also perforated. The vessel was slipped with red haematite & mica. A black mark on the side. Two knobs and raised bands of clay decorate the spout and neck area. The pattern impressed on the body during its rotation on a fibre pounding mat. [ASh [OPS move] 09/03/2016]
?Stone left when separating earth for making pottery slip.
Mica to be made into pottery slip.
Pot for holding water to wash a new baby with. [JP 29/3/2004]

masks-ritual.title: Incense burner of red ware. Bowl set on tall pedestal foot with expanded base and narrowing pillar. The rim of the bowl is slightly expanded. The interior and rim has been slipped with graphite and the exterior has a haemitite or mica slip. [MOBB [OPS move] 30/06/2016]

Incense burner. Made of beaten of clay tempered with organic matter, slipped with red haematite & mica. Rounded bowl for the body with a flared foot. Over the top of the bowl are three arches that conjoin in the centre above the bowl. Red interior. This vessel has a metallic slip on the entirety of the object. [Alicia Bell [OPS move] 28/06/2016]

Incense burner. Made of beaten clay. Pedestalled bowl with 3 handles arching upwards from the rim to meet over the centre. At this juncture there is a small hole. The body was slipped with red haematite & mica, & fired on its side for a red interior. Mat impression just visible. [Bethany Skuce OPS move] 28/06/2016]
